metadata.name: IVA-80: Indus Valley Civilization QA Benchmark

questions.q: Where is Mohenjo-daro located?
questions.ground_truth: Sindh province, Pakistan, on the right bank of the Indus river

questions.q: When was Harappa first excavated and by whom?
questions.ground_truth: 1920-21 by Daya Ram Sahni; followed by Vats from 1926

questions.q: What is unique about Dholavira's water management?
questions.ground_truth: 16 reservoirs cut into rock, three-tier division, stone construction

questions.q: What is Lothal's most distinctive feature?
questions.ground_truth: A massive brick-lined basin interpreted by S.R. Rao as a tidal dockyard (debated)

questions.q: What did Rakhigarhi's 2019 ancient DNA study find?
questions.ground_truth: No Steppe ancestry in Mature Harappan individuals (Shinde et al. 2019, Cell)

questions.q: What is the deepest pre-Harappan site?
questions.ground_truth: Mehrgarh in Balochistan, occupied from c.7000 BCE

questions.q: How wide are Mohenjo-daro's main streets?
questions.ground_truth: 9-10 m wide on cardinal axes

questions.q: What is the DK Area at Mohenjo-daro?
questions.ground_truth: Largest excavated section of the Lower Town, excavated by Mackay 1927-31

questions.q: What is the ploughed field at Kalibangan?
questions.ground_truth: World's earliest ploughed field, c.2800 BCE, with cross-ploughing pattern

questions.q: How many wells did Mohenjo-daro have?
questions.ground_truth: Approximately 700 documented wells, roughly one per three houses

questions.q: How many inscribed Indus seals have been catalogued?
questions.ground_truth: Approximately 4,000 in the CISI corpus

questions.q: What material were Indus seals made from?
questions.ground_truth: Steatite (soapstone), kiln-fired to harden

questions.q: What is the most common animal motif on Indus seals?
questions.ground_truth: The 'unicorn' (stylised one-horned bull), about 60% of figured seals

questions.q: What is seal M-304?
questions.ground_truth: The Pashupati seal from Mohenjo-daro, a horned seated figure surrounded by animals

questions.q: Who first interpreted M-304 as proto-Shiva?
questions.ground_truth: John Marshall in 1931

questions.q: What is the standard format of an Indus seal?
questions.ground_truth: 5-6 script signs above an animal motif with a 'feeding standard' object

questions.q: Have Indus seals been found in Mesopotamia?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, at Ur, Susa, Kish, and Tell Asmar

questions.q: What is the Ernestite drill?
questions.ground_truth: A precision drill type used by Harappans for carnelian bead-making

questions.q: What object accompanies the unicorn on most seals?
questions.ground_truth: A 'standard' or 'manger' - vertical pole with domed/cylindrical top

questions.q: What is the function of Indus seals?
questions.ground_truth: Administrative stamps pressed into clay bullae and tags to mark goods or transactions

questions.q: Has the Indus script been deciphered?
questions.ground_truth: No, it remains undeciphered

questions.q: How many distinct signs are in the Indus script?
questions.ground_truth: Approximately 400 distinct signs

questions.q: What is the most frequent sign in the Indus script?
questions.ground_truth: M-99, the 'jar' sign, ~1395 occurrences (Mahadevan 1977)

questions.q: What is the most common bigram in the Indus script?
questions.ground_truth: FISH followed by JAR (M-86 -> M-99), ~412 occurrences

questions.q: What is the average inscription length?
questions.ground_truth: About 4.6 signs; most inscriptions are under 7 signs

questions.q: What is Parpola's hypothesis about the script?
questions.ground_truth: It encodes a Dravidian language; the fish sign represents 'star/deity'

questions.q: What is Yajnadevam's claim?
questions.ground_truth: A computational decipherment proposing a Sanskrit-based reading of the script

questions.q: What did Rao et al. 2009 find about the script's entropy?
questions.ground_truth: Conditional entropy lies within natural-language range, refuting non-linguistic claims

questions.q: What direction is the Indus script read?
questions.ground_truth: Right-to-left, evidenced by sign cramping at line ends

questions.q: Where does the JAR sign typically appear?
questions.ground_truth: Final position - 84% terminal, likely a grammatical case marker

questions.q: What did Indus people trade with Mesopotamia?
questions.ground_truth: Carnelian beads, ivory, shell, hardwoods, possibly cotton; received silver, wool, tin

questions.q: What did Mesopotamians call the Indus region?
questions.ground_truth: Meluhha

questions.q: Where were Indus carnelian beads found in Mesopotamia?
questions.ground_truth: Royal Tombs of Ur, including Queen Puabi's tomb

questions.q: What is Dilmun?
questions.ground_truth: Bronze Age maritime entrepot at Bahrain, intermediate hub between Indus and Mesopotamia

questions.q: What is Magan?
questions.ground_truth: Bronze Age maritime hub at Oman, copper-rich, intermediate trade node

questions.q: What is Shortugai?
questions.ground_truth: Indus outpost on the Oxus river in Afghanistan, lapis lazuli source

questions.q: What is Sutkagan-Dor?
questions.ground_truth: Westernmost Indus outpost, on Makran coast of Balochistan

questions.q: What was the Indus standard weight?
questions.ground_truth: Cubical chert weight ~13.6 g, used as regional standard in Persian Gulf

questions.q: What is a Persian Gulf seal?
questions.ground_truth: Hybrid seal type blending Indus and local iconography, found at Mesopotamian sites

questions.q: What is the Meluhhan village at Lagash?
questions.ground_truth: Cuneiform-attested Indus expatriate settlement in southern Mesopotamia

questions.q: Did the Indus civilization have temples?
questions.ground_truth: No clearly identified temples; possible ritual structures (Great Bath, fire altars debated)

questions.q: What are the Kalibangan fire altars?
questions.ground_truth: Row of 7 brick-lined pits, possibly Vedic agnihotra-like ritual hearths (B.B. Lal interpretation)

questions.q: What is the proto-Shiva debate?
questions.ground_truth: Marshall's 1931 reading of M-304 as Shiva precursor; modern consensus is more cautious

questions.q: What is the pipal tree's significance?
questions.ground_truth: Sacred motif on seals and pottery; possibly an early form of the later sacred fig tradition

questions.q: What is the Great Bath?
questions.ground_truth: Watertight tank at Mohenjo-daro citadel, 12x7x2.4m, bitumen-sealed; likely ritual purification

questions.q: What are Harappan terracotta figurines?
questions.ground_truth: Female figurines with elaborate headdresses; called 'mother goddess' by Marshall, contested today

questions.q: Is the swastika motif found at Indus sites?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, on seals and pottery, predating Indo-Aryan period

questions.q: When did the Indus civilization decline?
questions.ground_truth: Beginning c.1900 BCE, completing by c.1300 BCE

questions.q: What was the 4.2 ka event?
questions.ground_truth: A global aridification c.2200-1900 BCE that weakened the SW monsoon

questions.q: What happened to the Ghaggar-Hakra river?
questions.ground_truth: Drying/shifting of the channel, reducing water for sites along its course

questions.q: What is Cemetery H?
questions.ground_truth: Late Harappan burial ground at Harappa, distinctive painted pottery, fractional burial

questions.q: Is the Indus decline attributed to Aryan invasion?
questions.ground_truth: No - the invasion theory is rejected; decline preceded Indo-Aryan arrival

questions.q: What are the Late Harappan regional cultures?
questions.ground_truth: Cemetery H, Jhukar, Rangpur - regional fragmentations after de-urbanisation

questions.q: What is the brick ratio used in Indus cities?
questions.ground_truth: 1:2:4 (thickness : width : length), maintained from Mohenjo-daro to Lothal

questions.q: What is the Indus drainage system?
questions.ground_truth: Covered brick drains under streets with manholes, household connections - earliest city-scale sanitation

questions.q: What is the two-mound plan?
questions.ground_truth: Raised western citadel with public buildings + larger eastern lower town

questions.q: How were Harappan bricks made?
questions.ground_truth: Wooden moulds, sun-dried then kiln-fired, English bond construction

questions.q: What was the role of the granary?
questions.ground_truth: Massive raised brick platform with air-channels; function debated (granary vs assembly hall)

questions.q: What is Cemetery R-37?
questions.ground_truth: Type-cemetery of Mature Harappan period at Harappa - extended burials with grave goods

questions.q: What are the Indus phases?
questions.ground_truth: Early (3300-2600 BCE), Mature (2600-1900 BCE), Late (1900-1300 BCE)

questions.q: Did the Indus civilization have horses?
questions.ground_truth: Domestic Equus caballus is rare/absent in Mature Harappan; appears reliably only post-1900 BCE

questions.q: Did the Indus civilization have kings?
questions.ground_truth: No clear evidence of kings; widely interpreted as corporate/heterarchical polity

questions.q: Was the Indus civilization militaristic?
questions.ground_truth: No clear evidence of warfare or weapons; described as 'urban but non-militaristic'

questions.q: What is the Aryan migration debate?
questions.ground_truth: Whether Indo-Aryan speakers migrated into post-Harappan India; aDNA evidence suggests post-1900 BCE entry from Steppe

questions.q: Who is the Priest-King statuette?
questions.ground_truth: DK 1909 stone bust from Mohenjo-daro, named by Marshall; identity unknown

questions.q: What is the Dancing Girl?
questions.ground_truth: Bronze figurine DK 5880, 10.5cm, lost-wax cast, female with bangles, hand on hip

questions.q: Was the Indus civilization literate?
questions.ground_truth: Yes - had a script with ~400 signs, ~4000 inscriptions; literacy extent unknown

questions.q: What was the Indus political organisation?
questions.ground_truth: Unknown but apparently non-monarchic; possibly trade-house councils or guild federations

questions.q: What does the unicorn motif represent?
questions.ground_truth: Likely a clan, guild, or administrative emblem - the most institutionally significant motif

questions.q: What is the zebu bull?
questions.ground_truth: Humped Indian bull, second most common seal motif after the unicorn

questions.q: What composite animals appear on seals?
questions.ground_truth: Hybrid creatures combining features of bull, elephant, tiger, etc.

questions.q: What are the Daimabad bronzes?
questions.ground_truth: Late Harappan bronze figurines from Daimabad, Maharashtra (chariot, elephant, buffalo, rhinoceros)

questions.q: Who is John Marshall?
questions.ground_truth: British archaeologist, ASI Director-General who excavated Mohenjo-daro 1922-27, published 3-volume report 1931

questions.q: Who is Iravatham Mahadevan?
questions.ground_truth: Indian epigraphist, compiled the canonical Indus Script Concordance (1977)

questions.q: Who is Asko Parpola?
questions.ground_truth: Finnish Indologist, edited the Corpus of Indus Seals and Inscriptions (CISI), proposed Dravidian decipherment

questions.q: Who is Jonathan Mark Kenoyer?
questions.ground_truth: American archaeologist, excavated Harappa, runs harappa.com, authored 'Ancient Cities' (1998)

questions.q: Who is Gregory Possehl?
questions.ground_truth: American archaeologist, authored 'The Indus Civilization: A Contemporary Perspective' (2002)

questions.q: Who is R.S. Bisht?
questions.ground_truth: Indian archaeologist who excavated Dholavira

questions.q: Who is Vasant Shinde?
questions.ground_truth: Indian archaeologist, lead on the 2019 Rakhigarhi ancient DNA study

questions.q: Who is B.B. Lal?
questions.ground_truth: Indian archaeologist, excavated Kalibangan, proposed Vedic-Harappan continuity hypothesis
